title: holloway-medtech-integration-scratch-journal
content:
Meeting capture -- Holloway MedTech initial integration (notes + rough action items)

Attendees: Ava (SE), Diego (SE), Priya (Customer PM), Ben (Holloway infra), Mira (Holloway ML eng)
Date: 2026-02-25 call, follow-ups 2026-03-10

Goal: fastpath a private Redwood deployment inside Holloway VPC for inference of triage assistant model. Primary constraints: PHI handling, on-prem-ish latency targets (p95 < 120ms for 512 tokens), and requirement to keep model weights within customer network.

What they said / requirements (paraphrased):
- Must not egress PHI; audit logs required for every inference call with correlation id.
- KMS-backed key storage, HSM optional for secrets. Need us to support customer KMS keys.
- Prefer dedicated GPU pool but host control plane must remain in Redwood-managed SaaS. They want traffic routed via private peering.
- Throughput: 40 concurrent sessions, avg prompt length ~250 tokens, bursts up to 120 sessions during morning triage window.
- Model family: huggingface-based 7B family (quantized) to start; may test 13B if latency ok.
- Prompting: heavy context stitching (previous messages + EHR snippets) — implies high prefix reuse and KV cache benefits.
- Compliance: SOC2 + HITRUST is their risk bar; they want a short compliance questionnaire for proof-of-concept.

Key technical gotchas called out during convo:
- Tokenization mismatch: customer uses legacy tokenizer for notes export, ML team said we must preserve whitespace/newline quirks. Need to validate token counts with our tokenizer vs their pipeline.
- KV cache warmup: large patient history will result in long first-token latencies. Consider setting warm-up priming requests or pre-populating cache on session creation.
- Sequence length: some EHR entries hit 8k chars; need to measure effective token length and decide truncation strategy. Truncation policy must be explicit in docs.
- Batching: their burst pattern is spiky (morning waves). Autoscaling + short queue window preferred to avoid 20s tails. Explore continuous batching with timeout of 5-8ms to keep latency tight.
- Fallbacks: they want deterministic fallback to smaller quantized model during overload rather than random degradation. We should propose model-variant routing by policy.

Preliminary architecture notes (working):
- Private control plane with VPC peering (AWS) + route-only peering to Redwood control endpoints. Data-plane (inference) runs in their VPC on customer-managed instances (or our private tenancy) — clarify ops ownership.
- Use customer KMS key for token encryption at rest; integrate with Redwood private KMS connector (doc link to share).
- Model artifacts: prefer S3 bucket behind customer account with restricted role for model pulls; automated checksum verification on pull.

Quick perf thought experiment (back-of-envelope):
- Target p95 120ms for 512 tokens. On A100-ish node, 7B q4_0 quantized should be ~40-70ms for 512 tokens depending on kernel set and prompt length. But with KV warmup overhead that could push 150-200ms for cold sessions. So emphasize cache pre-warm and pinned sessions for high-priority triage workflows.

Example API / integration notes (to share with Mira):
- Recommend route: POST /v1/private/infer?model=hf/holloway-7b-q4_0&session_id={s}
- Include header: X-Redwood-Correlation-Id and X-Redwood-Audit-Tag for linking to EHR id
- Sample fields: {"history": [...], "latest_note": "...", "patient_id": "...", "sensitive": true}
- We need to supply a short SDK snippet w/ presigned model pull example for their infra team.

Open questions (needs quick answers):
1) Who will operate the inference nodes? Holloway infra or Redwood private on-prem package? (Ben to confirm)
2) Do they have AWS PrivateLink or just VPC peering? PrivateLink would simplify control-plane connectivity.
3) HSM requirement: is HSM a hard requirement for POC or only for go-live? Priya said might be go-live only.
4) Expected retention window for logs (audit): 1y? 90 days? Compliance will require a recommendation.

Immediate next steps (owner + ETA):
- [Ava] Draft brief architecture diagram + short security checklist for POC (deliver by 2026-03-01).
- [Diego] Run quick tokenizer parity check: compare Redwood tokenizer token counts vs Holloway export for 50 sample EHR notes; deliver CSV of diffs (due 2026-03-03).
- [Ben - Holloway] Confirm infra ownership and whether they can host GPU nodes (answer 2026-03-05).
- [Priya] Share sample anonymized EHR snippet set (5 examples) and traffic profile CSV (due 2026-03-04).
- [Ava/Diego] Prototype cache prewarm logic, measure cold-first-token on 7B q4_0 locally; quick bench by 2026-03-07.
- [Ava] Prepare compliance questionnaire draft to accelerate procurement (by 2026-03-02).

Notes to self (quick heuristics / reminders):
- Keep sample prompts short in demo to avoid hitting TS/queue saturation on first run.
- When proposing model pinning, include simple rollback option (pin by tag + TTL).
- For audit logs, recommend immutable append-only store (S3 with object lock or similar) and separate key rotation schedule for PHI markers.

Risks:
- If Holloway insists on cold-starts for many sessions, meeting their p95 SLO will be expensive (need capacity + pinned instances).
- Tokenization mismatch could cause billing surprises and hallucination differences. Prioritize parity test.

Conversation fragments / raw snippets from Mira (copied as-is):
"We have a couple hundred long-form notes that are basically concatenated templates + free text. Tokenization throws off the ML team when punctuation runs together."
"If we can get 80% of morning triage under 100ms p95 we'd be ecstatic — failing that, we need clear expectation docs so clinicians don't mistrust latency."

Useful links to attach to POC packet:
- Redwood Private quickstart (internal link to share)
- Draft model-variant routing doc (CONFLUENCE-5682)
- Example presigned S3 role policy snippet (we will attach to PR)

Done-for-POC checklist (short):
- Tokenizer parity report
- 5 sample anonymized EHRs + traffic CSV
- KMS integration plan + KMS key policy draft
- Model artifact pull & checksum flow documented
- Baseline latency bench for cold + warm sessions on 7B quantized

BRIEF MEETING LOG / TIMELINE:
- 2026-02-25 initial call (this doc)
- 2026-03-08 tech sync to present tokenizer results + infra decision
- 2026-03-15 POC deploy window target (if infra confirmed)

Misc scratch (for later):
- Consider offering a tiny local inference shim that Holloway can run inside their network to handle pre-tokenization and prefix caching; would reduce our cold penalty and keep PHI on-prem.
- If they go 13B we need to recommend >2 GPUs per shard or use model-slicing to preserve latency.

-- end of scratch journal (keep updating here as answers come in)
